name: PID_Line_Tracer_V2
description: Improved dual-color-sensor PID line tracer using standard SPIKE-RT v0.2.0 APIs only. Startup mode menu: LEFT selects line tracing, RIGHT selects calibration, CENTER confirms. Calibration drives straight across a transverse black line from white to black to white and independently calibrates sensors B/F. Line tracing classifies centered, left-edge, right-edge, both-dark/crossing, and transition states. It also computes relative differential-drive wheel odometry (X/Y, heading, distance, speed, yaw rate, curvature) from A/E encoders using 88 mm wheels and 144 mm track, and uses measured yaw rate for conservative damping and speed adaptation. Includes a 10 ms cyclic notification, measured control interval, filtered derivative, conditional integral anti-windup, adaptive speed, and force sensor C start/stop. No driver modifications. The built-in SPIKE Prime LSM6DS3TR-C IMU is initialized using the standard hub_imu API; a stationary 3-axis gyro bias/noise estimate is recorded, and 3-axis acceleration/angular velocity are logged at 5 Hz alongside encoder-derived yaw rate. IMU data is diagnostic-only in this phase and is not yet fused into PID control.
warning: Calibration requires both color sensors to start on white, with the robot facing straight toward a black line that crosses the direction of travel. Keep the robot unobstructed during calibration. Odometry is relative and will drift with wheel slip or incorrect wheel geometry; it cannot identify absolute line position when both sensors see equal white. Verify wheel diameter/track width, motor direction, calibration thresholds, control timing, and PID/odometry gains on the actual robot. Keep the robot completely stationary during the approximately 1 second gyro-bias calibration. The IMU diagnostics are logged at 5 Hz and do not yet affect steering; compare gyro Z with encoder yaw before enabling sensor fusion.
